answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The mesa multiplier is published, charged in basalt, and tide lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3938 identities would post 3485 proofs and burn roughly 55 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
